definition: Anesthesia means a drug-induced loss of feeling or sensation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word anesthesia. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know anesthesia should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The boy was under anesthesia before the surgeons uncovered their tray, and he woke asking when the operation would begin.
Grogginess is far short of anesthesia — a foggy heaviness after poor sleep or a strong cold pill, with every sense still on duty and nothing switched off.
Sedation goes further than grogginess — the patient is calmed and drowsed on purpose — but anesthesia claims the most: sensation itself is switched off.

Numbness is the lost feeling itself, whatever caused it — a frozen bench, a pinched nerve, a foot gone to sleep. Anesthesia is that same absence created on purpose: a drug switches sensation off for a procedure and hands it back afterward. Numbness names the state; anesthesia names the engineered version.

A stupor is a dazed, barely-conscious fog — from illness, exhaustion, or drink — in which the senses still leak through. Anesthesia is precise and deliberate: a measured drug takes sensation away cleanly and returns it on schedule. A stupor happens to you; anesthesia is administered.

On an October morning in 1846, a Boston dentist named William Morton carried a glass flask into a hospital operating theater and changed surgery forever.
The patient inhaled ether fumes from the flask and drifted beyond reach.
A surgeon then removed a tumor from his neck while an audience of doctors waited for a scream.
The man woke minutes later and reported feeling nothing at all.
Newspapers called it the conquest of pain.
Physicians called the new practice anesthesia, and within a year it had crossed the Atlantic.
Surgery could finally slow down.
Operations that had been races against a patient's endurance became careful, deliberate work on a body that felt none of it.
